items.title: Why climate and health are connected
items.objectives: Short hosted Q&A establishing the basic exposure pathways between a warming climate and human health — heat, air quality, infectious disease shifts, food and water security — at an entry-level register suitable as a module opener.
items.audienceSummary: District and county health officers, programme managers, general health workforce, community audiences

items.title: What is the One Health Approach?
items.provider: Istituto Zooprofilattico Sperimentale delle Venezie (IZSVe) & FAO
items.objectives: Visualizes the interconnections between human welfare, domestic and wild animal reservoirs, and ecosystem integrity to prevent emerging zoonoses.
items.audienceSummary: Entry-level practitioners, interdisciplinary teams, community

items.title: Anticipatory Action and Community Preparedness in Flood-Prone Counties
items.provider: Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS) & County Government of Homa Bay
items.objectives: Highlights how the Kenya Anticipatory Action Roadmap and local Early Action Protocols trigger early funding, community evacuations, and water sanitation supplies ahead of Lake Victoria basin flooding.
items.audienceSummary: Disaster risk managers, county emergency planners, community health coordinators
items.accessLabel: Open Access / Embeddable (Kenya Red Cross Society YouTube)

items.title: Too Hot to Thrive: Heat Impacts on Maternal and Neonatal Health
items.objectives: Documents direct physiological heat stress, dehydration, and increased labor burdens among pregnant and postpartum women and neonates in Kilifi, Kenya.
items.audienceSummary: Midwives, maternal health clinicians, community nurses

items.title: How Does Ahmedabad's Heat Action Plan Help Deal with Climate Change?
items.provider: Carbon Brief & Indian Institute of Public Health Gandhinagar (IIPHG)
items.objectives: Dr. Abhiyant Tiwari explains the operational mechanics of converting heat forecasts into municipal response, including school schedule adjustments, drinking water points, and cool roofs.
items.audienceSummary: Local adaptation managers, urban health officers, municipal planners
items.accessLabel: Open Access / CC BY-NC (Carbon Brief YouTube)

items.title: Management of Heat Stroke (mockdrill) | लू तापघात प्रबंधन (पूर्वाभ्यास)
items.objectives: Hindi-language ward-level simulation of heat stroke response — recognition, rapid cooling, triage sequence and staff roles — usable as a rehearsal template before heat season rather than a lecture on heat illness.
items.audienceSummary: PHC and CHC clinical staff, nursing and emergency room teams, district heat-season trainers
items.accessLabel: Open Access (Rajasthan DMHFW YouTube) — embed status unverified

items.title: Heat-Related Illness and Death Surveillance training
items.objectives: Walks through NHRIDS reporting — case definitions for heat-related illness and death, daily summer reporting formats, and portal submission workflow during the declared heat season.
items.audienceSummary: District surveillance officers, NPCCHH state and district nodal officers, epidemiologists, hospital records and IDSP staff
items.accessLabel: Open Access (NPCCHH / NCDC / MoHFW YouTube) — embed status unverified

items.title: Climate Change, Health Equity, and Extreme Weather across Africa
items.provider: Columbia University GCCHE & African Population and Health Research Center (APHRC)
items.objectives: Explores hydrometeorological extremes, inland flooding, drought-driven food insecurity, and particulate air pollution across East Africa, focusing on maternal-child vulnerability and public health leadership.
items.audienceSummary: African health professionals, environmental health officers, climate negotiators

items.title: Climate Change and Health: An Overview of Global Threats and Responses
items.objectives: Synthesizes primary direct and indirect exposure pathways, climate-induced disease burdens, and health co-benefits generated through mitigation sectors.
items.audienceSummary: Public health workforce, municipal planners, students

items.title: Climate Change and Health: Clinical Implications and Systemic Stresses
items.objectives: Details clinical surges during extreme heat, facility power failures, and the imperative for redirecting climate adaptation finance toward health systems.
items.audienceSummary: Clinicians, hospital directors, health system planners

items.title: The Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change: Global Launch Debrief
items.objectives: Longitudinal tracking of global heat-related mortality, food insecurity trajectories, fossil fuel health burdens, and health adaptation financing shortfalls.
items.audienceSummary: Academic researchers, epidemiologists, policy directors

items.title: Health and Climate: Shaping a Resilient and Equitable Future
items.provider: WHO European Centre for Environment and Health
items.objectives: Outlines systemic adaptation, low-carbon healthcare operations, legislative reforms, and targeted protections for vulnerable demographics.
items.audienceSummary: Environmental health officers, municipal authorities, health delegates

items.title: Advancing Global Public Health through Planetary Health and One Health
items.provider: World Federation of Public Health Associations (WFPHA) & Planetary Health Alliance
items.objectives: Clarifies definitions and operational commonalities between One Health and Planetary Health paradigms across climate, biodiversity, and disease spillovers.
items.audienceSummary: Public health faculty, environmental epidemiologists
items.accessLabel: Open Access / Embeddable (Planetary Health Alliance YouTube)

items.title: Integrating the Environment into One Health: The Quadripartite Vision
items.objectives: Focuses on Action Track 6 of the One Health Joint Plan of Action, identifying institutional mechanisms to embed ecosystem data into disease prevention.
items.audienceSummary: Environmental regulators, veterinary authorities, public health leads

items.title: Cross-Sectoral Data Architecture for One Health Implementation
items.provider: DHIS2 & Health Information Systems Programme (HISP Centre)
items.objectives: Demonstrates integrated digital pipelines combining event-based surveillance, livestock disease reporting, and climate variables to dissolve departmental silos.
items.audienceSummary: Health informaticians, surveillance officers, data architects
items.accessLabel: Open Access / CC BY-SA (DHIS2 Learning Platform)

items.title: Implementing Health in All Policies: Co-Benefits Across Sectors
items.provider: European Observatory on Health Systems and Policies
items.objectives: Examines institutional alignment across healthcare, climate planning, housing, and civil infrastructure, demonstrating shared economic returns.
items.audienceSummary: Municipal executives, urban planners, budget directors

items.title: Climate, Health, and Equity in All Policies: The California Framework
items.provider: CivicWell & California Department of Public Health (CDPH)
items.objectives: Practical review of the CDPH Climate Change and Health Equity Branch collaborating with housing, transport, and energy agencies on general plan updates.
items.audienceSummary: State/local policymakers, regional planning councils

items.title: Operationalizing Intersectoral Public Health Strategies
items.provider: National Collaborating Centre for Healthy Public Policy (NCCHPP Canada)
items.objectives: Features public health leaders detailing lessons learned in cross-departmental coalition building, communication strategies, and health advocacy.
items.audienceSummary: Local public health practitioners, municipal leads

items.title: Health in All Policies: A Guide for State and Local Governments
items.provider: American Public Health Association (APHA) & Public Health Institute
items.objectives: Translates published HiAP guidance into concrete institutional mechanisms, including health impact assessments, interagency agreements, and zoning reforms.
items.audienceSummary: Agency heads, intersectoral task forces, policy analysts

items.title: Navigating the Climate Health and Risk Tool: Spatial Risk to Interventions
items.objectives: Detailed platform walkthrough demonstrating how hierarchical fuzzy logic models combine hazard, exposure, and vulnerability into intervention menus.
items.audienceSummary: GIS analysts, climate adaptation managers, health officers
tags: External tool sharing the CHART name

items.title: Heat Action Planning for Local Health Departments: The CHaRT Platform
items.objectives: Dr. Jeremy Hess presents the randomized controlled trial of CHaRT across 30 health departments, covering workflows, intervention catalogs, and funding preparation.
items.audienceSummary: Local health department leadership, emergency managers
tags: External tool sharing the CHART name

items.title: From Vulnerability Indexing to Evidence-Based Heat Interventions
items.provider: UW School of Public Health & Public Health – Seattle & King County
items.objectives: Reviews the Auburn, WA pilot showing how CHaRT vulnerability indicators (e.g., mobile homes, poverty) guided cooling resources and utility energy-burden relief.
items.audienceSummary: Municipal resilience officers, electric utilities, program managers

items.title: Building the Case for Translational Research and Community Action
items.objectives: Instructs applicants on leveraging CHART pilot ($20,000) and community ($5,000) grants to generate preliminary data and community partnerships for larger NIH grants.
items.audienceSummary: Academic researchers, community organizations, grant writers
tags: External tool sharing the CHART name

items.title: Specialized Training Module: Anticipatory Action and Anticipatory Finance
items.provider: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR)
items.objectives: Explains the shift from reactive disaster response to early intervention using impact-based forecasting, pre-agreed triggers, and pre-arranged financing pools.
items.audienceSummary: Disaster risk coordinators, humanitarian finance officers

items.title: The Fundamentals of Anticipatory Action: Design, Triggers, and Timing
items.objectives: In-depth workshop covering trigger threshold calibration, standard operating procedures, early action design, and delineating response transitions.
items.audienceSummary: Operational planners, national meteorological agencies, Red Cross delegates

items.title: Forecast-Based Financing: Mechanics of Early Action Protocols
items.provider: IFRC & Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre
items.objectives: Visualizes how risk maps and weather forecasts trigger automated funding disbursements and Early Action Protocols prior to hazard impact.
items.audienceSummary: Field operatives, disaster management committees, public

items.title: Anticipatory Action and the Grand Bargain: Unlocking Global Finance
items.objectives: Analyzes donor mechanisms, institutional funding bottlenecks, and strategies for scaling pre-arranged finance across national disaster frameworks.
items.audienceSummary: Multilateral donors, budget analysts, policy advocates

items.title: Climate Disruption, Maternal Vulnerability, and Obstetric Care
items.provider: International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO)
items.objectives: Examines clinical evidence linking extreme heat and air pollution to preterm delivery, preeclampsia, and stillbirth, offering adaptive clinical care pathways.
items.audienceSummary: Obstetricians, gynecologists, maternal-fetal medicine teams
items.accessLabel: Open Access / Embeddable (FIGO / Climate for Health)

items.title: Public Health Practices to Support Community Recovery Post-Flooding
items.provider: NCCEH Canada & PolicyWise for Children & Families
items.objectives: Focuses on community-level flood recovery, indoor mold remediation, private well disinfection, and managing long-term psychosocial trauma and anxiety.
items.audienceSummary: Environmental health officers, municipal recovery teams

items.title: Public Health Impacts of Compound Drought and Heatwaves
items.provider: California Department of Public Health (CDPH) & CARB
items.objectives: Evaluates public health hazards from concurrent drought and heat, such as elevated particulate dust ($PM_{10}$/$PM_{2.5}$), water scarcity, and interagency response plans.
items.audienceSummary: Epidemiologists, air quality specialists, water regulators

items.title: Julia Gillard launches the Lancet Countdown 2025
items.objectives: Short launch announcement framing the 2025 Lancet Countdown findings. Cited in the source doc (ref 8) as the basis for the Lancet Countdown row, but not the video actually linked in that row.
items.audienceSummary: General audiences, advocacy

items.title: The 2025 Global Report of the Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change
items.objectives: Full presentation of the 2025 global report indicators. Complements (and is more current than) the 2024 launch debrief already in the sheet.
items.audienceSummary: Academic researchers, epidemiologists, policy directors

items.title: The role of the health sector in tackling climate change (SDG13)
items.objectives: Positions the health sector's own mitigation and advocacy role within SDG13. Cited in the source doc (ref 24) but not mapped to any curriculum row.
items.audienceSummary: Health system leaders, policy analysts

items.title: Anticipatory action: an introduction
items.objectives: Entry-level introduction to anticipatory action. Likely the better short-form opener for this module than the 75-min workshop currently listed.
items.audienceSummary: Disaster risk coordinators, humanitarian staff

items.title: Anticipatory action: How the Pacific stays one step ahead of disasters
items.objectives: Regional case study of anticipatory action in practice - the only non-Global/non-Northern example available for this module.
items.audienceSummary: National disaster agencies, programme managers

items.title: Professor Jane Hirst: Protecting pregnant women and babies from extreme heat
items.objectives: Clinical expert perspective on heat risk in pregnancy and protective care. Cited in the source doc (ref 49) but not mapped to a curriculum row.
items.audienceSummary: Obstetricians, midwives, maternal health programme staff

items.title: Climate Heat Maternal and Neonatal Health Africa (CHAMNHA) - project overview
items.objectives: Consortium overview of the CHAMNHA evidence base. Sits behind the 'Too Hot to Thrive' documentary already in the sheet and gives the research framing.
items.audienceSummary: Researchers, maternal health clinicians, community nurses

items.title: Ahmedabad’s Heat Action Plan: The First Early Warning System in South Asia
items.objectives: Documents South Asia's first municipal Heat Action Plan after the deadly 2010 heatwave, demonstrating color-coded warnings, cool roof rollouts, and hospital surge management.
items.audienceSummary: Municipal commissioners, disaster management authorities, public health directors

items.title: Protecting Workers in Heat Action Plans: Perspectives from Ahmedabad and Boston
items.provider: Harvard Mittal South Asia Institute, IIPHG, & SEWA
items.objectives: Connects occupational health, urban planning, and labor rights; features Dr. Dileep Mavalankar (IIPHG) and SEWA leadership on protecting women street vendors and outdoor laborers under heat stress.
items.audienceSummary: Labor inspectors, urban planners, public health officials, informal labor advocates

items.title: Rx Climate Prescriptions: Pathways for Climate Action by Indian Healthcare
items.provider: Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI) & Centre for Environmental Health
items.objectives: Details climate health vulnerabilities in India, from severe air pollution to thermal stress, and demonstrates decarbonization and climate-resilient hospital infrastructure.
items.audienceSummary: Clinicians, hospital administrators, national health mission directors

items.title: Animal Health Under a Worsening Climate Crisis: One Health in Practice
items.objectives: Evaluates pastoralist and agro-pastoralist communities in northern Kenya facing recurrent drought and erratic rainfall, focusing on livestock nutrition, vector shifts, and zoonotic disease control.
items.audienceSummary: Veterinary scientists, epidemiologists, agricultural officers, One Health leads

items.title: Integrated Drought Response and Climate-Smart Livelihoods in Arid Lands
items.objectives: Demonstrates slow-onset drought mitigation in semi-arid Kenya, utilizing satellite forecasting for early seed distributions, water harvesting, and nutrition surveillance to prevent acute malnutrition.
items.audienceSummary: Humanitarian officers, public health teams, rural development planners
items.accessLabel: Open Access / Embeddable (Kenya Red Cross Society YouTube)
